impTopics.title: Biological Nitrogen Fixation by Soil Microbes

These bacteria, known as biological nitrogen fixers, can help plants access nitrogen for growth. Additionally, nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria, such as blue-green algae, can release nitrogen that plants can reuse, contributing to soil fertility.

Examples of microorganisms include fungi that grow on bread, which can be seen with a magnifying glass, while others require a microscope to be observed due to their small size.

impTopics.title: Importance of Vaccines in Protecting Children from Diseases
impTopics.description: Vaccines are essential for protecting children from various diseases by stimulating the production of antibodies in the body to fight off disease-causing microbes. Antibiotics, on the other hand, are not effective against viruses like the common cold and flu. Vaccines, such as the polio drops given under the Pulse Polio Programme, have been instrumental in eradicating diseases like smallpox worldwide.
